business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture and Aseptic Tubing of Ambient Quick-Cook Tapioca Pearls

Convention between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation on Income (signed 3 April 1996; as amended by Protocol signed 25 June 2009)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 3 July 2023 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended, which recast the former Law of 12 November 2004; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019 on RBE registration, access and fees; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended; CSSF Circular 18/698 on AML/CFT compliance; transposition instruments for EU Directive 2015/849, Directive 2018/843 and Directive 2018/1673; Criminal Code provisions on money laundering and terrorist financing.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of a valid passport or national identity card of each individual ultimate beneficial owner of the SCSp
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's country of residence; for documents originating in the People's Republic of China, the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs or its designated apostille office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961) where the origin country is a Contracting State; otherwise Consular Legalization through the Luxembourg embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and complete memorandum and articles of association of any corporate general partner or corporate UBO holding 25% or more of the SCSp
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Original company registry of the corporate owner (e.g., State Administration for Market Regulation of the People's Republic of China or equivalent foreign registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization, in each case through the competent authority of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / official company register extract for each foreign corporate UBO or corporate general partner, issued not earlier than 90 days before filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Original corporate registry of the country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing Luxembourg avocat-à-la-cour / notary to incorporate the SCSp and to file all RCS and RBE declarations
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of the grantor and, where required, the local competent authentication authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Legalized source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declaration signed by each UBO, coupled with independent supporting documentation, required where any UBO qualifies as a PEP or is resident in a higher-risk jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public and financial institution or certified accountant in the UBO's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-onboarding and continuous screening of all individual UBOs, general partners, directors, authorized signatories and any person exercising control over more than 10% of the SCSp against: (i) Luxembourg national freezing decisions, (ii) the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, (iii) United Nations Security Council sanctions regimes, (iv) the OFAC SDN list and sectoral sanctions as best-practice for USD clearing, (v) Interpol notices, (vi) the Luxembourg Ministry of Foreign Affairs national listing, and (vii) adverse media/PEP databases. Foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, family members and close associates must be subject to enhanced due diligence, with written source-of-wealth and source-of-funds analysis before incorporation. Screening must be repeated at least daily after initial onboarding and must be documented in an audit trail retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) electronic filing and search portal, accessible via https://www.lbr.lu and https://www.ejustice.public.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Constitutional documents must be drafted in French, German or Luxembourgish; in practice French is used for RCS filings. The company name must appear in the Latin alphabet. If the commercial name originates in a non-Latin script (e.g., Chinese), an exact phonetic and legally distinct Latin-alphabet transliteration must be adopted and a certified French translation of the deed is mandatory. The name must include either the full words 'société en commandite spéciale' or the statutory abbreviation 'SCSp' immediately after the company-specific element. The name may not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing RCS-registered name and must not mislead as to the legal form, business purpose or public status of the entity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 'Banque', 'Bank', 'Bancaire', or any banking/financial intermediation term requiring prior CSSF authorization
'Assurance', 'Insurance', 'Rèassurance', or any insurance-sector term requiring prior CAA authorization
'Fonds', 'Fund', 'SIF', 'SICAV', 'SICAR', or regulated fund terminology requiring CSSF licensing
'Fiduciaire' or 'Fiduciary' without a licensed trust or fiduciary undertaking
'Luxembourg', 'Grand-Duché de Luxembourg', or 'Grand-Ducal' where the name would improperly imply official sponsorship
'Ministère', 'Administration', 'Police', 'Interpol', 'Europol', 'Armée', 'Gendarmerie', 'Croix-Rouge', 'United Nations' or other state, international or emblems protected by law
Any term contrary to public order (ordre public) or to bonnes mœurs
Any name producing confusion with the partnership's commercial purpose or with a protected trademark or registered domain of a third party
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No formal statutory name-reservation system exists in Luxembourg; the name becomes protected only upon effective RCS registration of the SCSp. If the RCS registrar rejects the proposed name due to identity, confusion or prohibited token, the applicant may: (i) submit a written request for informal registry review through the LBR MyBusiness portal within 15 calendar days of the refusal; (ii) if the refusal is maintained, file a formal administrative appeal before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg, commercial chamber, within one month of notification, represented by a Luxembourg avocat-à-la-cour; (iii) where the refusal concerns a sensitive token, obtain the prior no-objection letter from the competent ministry or CSSF/CAA before refiling; (iv) alternatively, amend the constitutional deed by a new notarial or private deed selecting a compliant name and proceed with a fresh RCS filing. The one-month court deadline may not be extended, but a new name application may be resubmitted immediately following a definitive refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole arrangement for an ISIC 1030 food-manufacturing SCSp. A virtual office or licensed domiciliation agent address may be used for RCS correspondence and general-partner administrative receipt only if the agent is supervised and physically located in Luxembourg. However, the SCSp must maintain a real and identifiable place of effective management in Luxembourg for tax and commercial substance. For the active canned boba/tapioca pearl manufacturing scope, all production, food-safety and product-liability obligations require a separately registered operating establishment or documented third-party toll manufacturing contract; a purely virtual presence would constitute abuse of law and will not pass AML/KYB bank due diligence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35-40% first-year probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by the Luxembourg tax authorities, RCS or the food-safety authority (ASTF) if operating activity or production contracts are booked in the SCSp; less than 10% for a dormant or passive holding SCSp with no Luxembourg operating assets.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / RCS public search portal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Free official online search; no statutory charge for preliminary screening

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark flat fee for name-clearance advisory

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial or private-deed constitutional documentation for the SCSp, including UBO declaration review and general-partner qualification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial fee band based on complexity; not a fixed statutory tariff for SCSp formation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS initial registration fee for filing the SCSp constitutional deed and appointment of general partner
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Grand-ducal regulatory fee schedule for electronic initial registration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the constitution in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: LBR fee schedule for electronic UBO declaration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of non-French apostilled constitutional documents, passports, powers of attorney and corporate extracts
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator admitted before Luxembourg courts
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Court-approved translator tariff and prevailing market page rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official consular and apostille fee schedules; notarial disbursements

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation PEP, OFAC, UN, EU and domestic sanctions screening with written risk memo
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing hourly rate (EUR 350-500/hour) capped as flat due-diligence fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg registered-office service for one quarter with mail handling, if outsourced to a licensed domiciliation agent pending operational setup
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for first-quarter corporate domiciliation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 102 et seq., as amended by the Law of 23 July 2016 introducing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 July 2016 on commercial register filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), operating the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) — Trade and Companies Register of Luxembourg, e-filing portal www.lbr.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Deed of constitution of the SCSp (pacte statutaire / contrat de société) together with the electronic application for registration (demande d'immatriculation) filed with the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an SCSp; contributions are fixed solely in the partnership agreement and may be in cash or in kind. Luxembourg law imposes no escrow account requirement; capital call and drawdown mechanics are governed by the partnership agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned board members of the General Partner of the SCSp resolve unanimously: (1) the partnership agreement, as signed by the initial partners, is approved, and the subscription of partnership interests with the agreed capital contributions is accepted; (2) the registered office is adopted at [Address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; (3) [Name] is appointed manager with sole-signature authority, and any two officers jointly may bind the partnership; (4) the manager is authorized to complete filings with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register and arrange publication in the official electronic gazette. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and notarial authentication of the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public; alternatively a private deed executed with qualified electronic signatures accepted by Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Luxembourg notary to draft the partnership agreement (pacte statutaire) in compliance with Articles 102 et seq. of the Law of 10 August 1915. The deed must identify the general partner and each initial limited partner, contribution amounts and drawdown mechanics, profit-sharing and loss allocation, management and voting rights, transfer restrictions, and the registered office in Luxembourg. Execute the deed before the notary or by private deed with qualified e-signatures, initial each schedule, and obtain the authentic act number.
required_dossiers: Notarized partnership agreement (pacte statutaire) or privately signed deed with qualified electronic signatures
Certified copies of passports or national identity cards of all founding partners and the general partner
Proof of registered office (lease agreement or domiciliation agreement)
Pro-forma first board resolution of the general partner
Bank reference or IBAN for capital contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or RCS pre-filing checks identify defective or incomplete clauses, amend the deed by a supplemental notarial act (acte rectificatif) and re-present the execution pages; where only annexes are missing, lodge the annexes within 5 business days to avoid refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), e-filing platform www.lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the authenticated partnership agreement, the RCS application form, signatory declarations, and registered office proof via the LBR e-filing interface. Pay the RCS registration fee online. Monitor the case in the LBR user workspace. Upon clearance, download the RCS certificate of registration with the Luxembourg registration number (numéro d'immatriculation).
required_dossiers: Authenticated partnership agreement (notarial or QES-signed PDF)
Specimen signatures and declaration of authorized signatories
Identity copies of all partners, the general partner, and the manager
Proof of registered office (lease, domiciliation agreement, notary consent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises a query (prise de conclusions), file a rectification within the one-month statutory window; if the deadline is missed, refile the complete dossier and request a waiver of late fees by demonstrating good faith and prompt cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the statutory extract in the RESA official electronic gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA), official electronic gazette administered by the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice and operated through LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, verify that LBR publishes the legal extract in RESA. Confirm that the published text matches the registered deed (parties, contributions, registered office, managers). Download and archive the RESA publication certificate to evidence third-party opposability.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA text is inaccurate, request LBR to republish a corrected extract; if publication is overdue, escalate via LBR support and preserve evidence of the initial publication time for legal effectiveness.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration: VAT, direct tax, and municipal business tax formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD); joint eCDF portal of the Luxembourg tax authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File VAT Form 1619 with the AEDT to obtain a Luxembourg VAT identification number for manufacturing and sales activities. Submit the SCSp partnership agreement and partner tax data; since the SCSp is fiscally transparent, income is allocated to partners. Register the employing entity (the general partner, if staffed) for payroll withholding and social security with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale.
required_dossiers: Tax identification numbers of the general partner and pass-through partners
Description of manufacturing and aseptic-tubing activities
Opening balance sheet or budget and bank IBAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT rejects or queries the VAT application, respond to the request for information within 15 days with corrected forms; if no VAT number issues within 30 days, send a formal reminder by registered letter to the AEDT registration service and request an official attestation of filing.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes and NIF issuance; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT registration, eTVA returns and registration duties; Administration des douanes et accises (ADA) for customs and export formalities. Official portals: MyGuichet.lu, eCDF, eTVA and guichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Before commencing taxable activity, the SCSp must be registered in the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCSL). For VAT, the SCSp or its statutory representative files the VAT registration application with the AEDT; non-established EU suppliers may use OSS/IOSS for distance sales, while non-EU suppliers generally must appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative and register from the first taxable euro. The ACD issues the 13-digit matricule (NIF) for direct tax compliance; the SCSp holds a NIF notwithstanding its tax-transparent status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: the SCSp is mandatorily transparent for Luxembourg corporate income tax and net wealth tax, with partners taxed on their allocable share of income and gains; it constitutes a distinct taxable person for VAT purposes; the SCSp has no legal personality and no minimum capital requirement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Luxembourg; SCSp transparency is mandatory and cannot be waived. Relevant statutory mechanisms include the VAT grouping election under Article 60 of the LTVL for closely-linked Luxembourg taxable persons, the freedom in the partnership deed to allocate profit shares binding Luxembourg direct tax allocation, and the corporate fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) election, which is unavailable to transparent SCSp taxpayers. EU ATAD hybrid and reverse-hybrid mismatch rules apply automatically to neutralise divergent cross-border classifications.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA) under the amended Luxembourg VAT Law (LTVL) implementing the EU VAT Directive.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for the domestic small-business (franchise) exemption, applicable only to Luxembourg-established businesses; exceeding the threshold triggers compulsory registration from the first euro. Non-established foreign suppliers have no local threshold, and EU distance sellers may use the EUR 10,000 EU-wide annual distance-sales threshold unless they opt for the OSS scheme or local Luxembourg registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2G e-invoicing via the PEPPOL network (PEPPOL BIS 3.0 / Factur-X) for invoices rendered under public procurement contracts; no real-time B2B fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control or digital stamping of commercial invoices is currently in force; compliance is ensured through eTVA returns, SAF-T audit files, EC Sales Lists and customs export records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for (i) exports of canned tapioca pearls physically dispatched or transported outside the EU, evidenced by an export declaration and transport proof, and (ii) intra-Community supplies to EU VAT-registered customers where a valid customer VAT ID is held, the goods leave Luxembourg, and the recapitulative statement is duly filed. Closely related offshore services such as packing and logistics are zero-rated when directly linked to the exported goods; other B2B services follow the reverse-charge place-of-supply rule.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic export declaration and exit confirmation via the Luxembourg and European customs system)
Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document (CMR, airway bill) evidencing physical removal of the goods from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank or treasury evidence confirming repatriation of export proceeds within the FX deadline)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may jointly verify export evidence with the customs authority; insufficient, false or fraudulent substantiation triggers reassessment of Luxembourg VAT at the domestic rate (17% standard or the applicable food rate), statutory default interest at 0.6% per month, late-payment surcharges and administrative fines, with criminal prosecution available in fraud cases; previously granted zero-rated refunds and input VAT credits are retrospectively clawed back within the statutory prescription periods, and the customs export confirmation may itself be revoked upon verification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) together with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) as the primary banks and financial markets supervisors under the Luxembourg law of 21 December 2018 and the CSSF Law of 12 July 2013.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a full member of the EU Economic and Monetary Union. The euro is freely convertible and there are no exchange controls on either current account or capital account transactions. The free movement of capital and payments is guaranteed under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. Profit remittance to non-resident partners is permitted without prior approval; however, dividend-like distributions to certain investors may trigger Luxembourg withholding tax unless an exemption under the participation exemption regime, a tax treaty, or an EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive applies. The SCSp is tax-transparent, and its partners are taxed at partner level; there are no statutory hurdles to profit repatriation beyond standard documentary evidence of distribution approval and substance substantiation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no export proceeds surrender requirement. Sellers may retain export income in any currency, convert it at free-market rates, and use it freely. There is no mandated percentage or statutory timeline for repatriation into euro, and no obligation to deposit funds with the BCL or a licensed bank beyond standard anti-money laundering (AML) record-keeping under Luxembourg law of 12 November 2004, as amended.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: The viability of using an offshore electronic money institution (EMI) is Medium with significant legal constraints. Under PSD2 and the CSSF's E-Money Regulations, only EU/EEA-licensed EMIs that have successfully completed a passport notification to Luxembourg (or have an establishment in Luxembourg) may operate. A non-EEA offshore EMI cannot provide services to a Luxembourg SCSp without a banking or payment-services license in Luxembourg. The SCSp should treat non-EU EMIs as ineligible for capital custody and trade settlement because they are not subject to BCL prudential supervision; where a fintech solution is desired, an EU-licensed EMI with a valid Luxembourg passport and a segregated client-funds account is acceptable for transactional flows only and not for escrow of partnership capital.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg legislation does not mandate an in-person physical interview for SCSp account opening. CSSF AML/KYC rules allow remote digital onboarding using video identification and electronic signatures provided the bank applies the prescribed technical and procedural safeguards (Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02). In practice, Tier-1 banks commonly require physical appearance or notarized/certified identification for the general partner, the ultimate beneficial owners, and the authorized signatories where the ownership chain is complex, the SCSp has non-EU partners, or the transaction profile involves high-risk jurisdictions. Remote opening is feasible if the company can supply apostilled powers of attorney, independent certificate of incorporation, and a video verification of the general partner's representative; nevertheless, the bank's internal risk committee may still request a documentary or physical interview before activating credit or disbursement functionality.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transparent partnership structure: SCSp has no legal personality and is treated as a contractual partnership, making it difficult for banks to identify who owns the assets and who is the legal account-holder.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the fully signed and notarized limited partnership agreement (contrat de société), a detailed list of partners and contribution amounts, beneficial ownership declarations, and a written explanation of the SCSp's commercial rationale. Include the certificate of registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), and corporate resolutions appointing the general partner and authorized signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital subscription from a non-EU related party: banks will flag cross-border wire transfers into a newly formed SCSp as potential layering in an unregulated vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble source-of-funds documentation from all investing partners: bank statements, audit reports, tax returns, proof of business license, and confirmation of legitimate origin of funds for the last 12–24 months. Provide the subscription agreement, notarized minutes approving capital increases, and the downstream commercial contracts showing the intended use of funds for the canned boba tapioca pearls manufacturing and aseptic tubing operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unregulated status: the SCSp is not a regulated financial entity, and bank compliance may classify it as a high-risk commercial partnership due to possible private-equity or investment-holding usage.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the detailed business plan for the manufacture and aseptic tubed ambient quick-cook tapioca pearls, evidence of physical substance such as a lease agreement for business premises in Luxembourg, payroll records or expected headcount, and the statutory director and partner financial statements. Any document proving local substance, operational activity, and real economic purpose will satisfy the suspicious activity review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mixed cross-border payment flows: future receipts and disbursements will involve EUR/USD conversion, fast-moving trade payments, and potentially third-party settlements with Asian suppliers, leading to a money-laundering territory mismatch alert.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a transactional forecast showing the clearing rails, expected counterparty list, and purpose of each payment leg, backed by purchase orders, invoices, and packaging / freight documents for the boba tapioca pearls supply chain. Banks will accept the dossier if it demonstrates legitimate trade and clear flows through the SCSp as a wafer-thin partnership vehicle.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The SCSp capital contributions may be wired from international investors to a Luxembourg bank account using standard SWIFT MT103 messages. The remitter should populate purpose code F2 (Direct investment) and include narrative: 'Capital contribution to an SCSp under Luxembourg law' with the unique partner identification if available. Where the foreign partner uses an OECD harmonised transaction system, the BOP code 'S121' or 'S12' (capital transfers) is acceptable if the bank accepts those values. The receiving bank must complete the CSSF-mandated customer due diligence before the first credit. For high-value injections, a signed capital subscription agreement, bank account confirmation letter, partnership deed, and proof of tax residence of the investor are required. The Luxembourg bank will release the funds only after verifying it is a genuine equity contribution and not a loan; if loan classification is intended, appropriate loan documentation and a substance-based explanation for the debt-to-equity ratio should be provided.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for sourcing tapioca pearls, packaging materials, aseptic tubing equipment, and commissioned manufacturing services may be executed through SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA trade partners (e.g., Asian noodle and pearl manufactures) and through SEPA credit transfer with fully structured remittance information for intra-EU suppliers. For larger contract values, a commercial documentary letter of credit (LC) issued by the Luxembourg bank by SWIFT MT700 is used to finance and reinsure the purchase of goods from high-risk jurisdictions. Payments should be routed through TARGET2 for EUR liquidity clearing, with the bank applying Luxembourg Treasury reporting under CSSF transparency rules. Trade settlement must be supported by invoices, airway bills, bills of lading, inspection certificates, and customs declarations to avoid anti-money-laundering charges.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable euro-forward contracts against major trade currencies (GBP, CHF, JPY, CNY where the counterparty can deliver)
FX options (call/put on EUR vs USD) for purchase of imported boba raw materials
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currencies that are not deliverable in Luxembourg, such as offshore RMB if commercial justification exists
Commodity-linked derivatives only where notified to CSSF where relevant and subject to EMIR reporting through a licensed clearing member

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership data (RBE confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (LBR/RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the LBR annual electronic reminder; annual anniversary of the initial RBE registration, or earlier upon any change in beneficial ownership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal reminder followed by administrative fine up to EUR 1,250 for first breach; up to EUR 12,500 for repeated breaches within five years; knowingly false statements may attract criminal fines and imprisonment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts and auditor's report (only if the SCSp exceeds publication and audit thresholds, or if consolidated into a corporate general partner's filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the balance sheet date (shareholders/general partner meeting within six months and RCS filing within one month thereafter); no fixed calendar date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Judicial injunction to file, court-imposed penalty payment up to EUR 500 per day of delay (commonly capped at EUR 10,000); repeated non-compliance may lead to removal from the RCS and liability of the general partner.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is triggered if the SCSp qualifies as a large undertaking on two consecutive balance sheet dates: balance sheet total above EUR 4.4 million; net turnover above EUR 8.8 million; average headcount above 50 employees. A SCSp may also be audited when its corporate general partner is legally subject to audit and consolidates the SCSp.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg statutory accounting rules (Lux GAAP) derived from the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies and the Law of 19 December 2002, implementing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS permitted only where elected for audited or consolidated accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner must keep the RBE declaration continuously accurate; any transfer of partnership interests or change of beneficial owner must be rectified within one month. Annually, the LBR sends a confirmation email and the registered agent or general partner must log into the RBE portal, check the stored data, and confirm its accuracy. A confirmation acknowledgement is produced after successful submission.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (limited and general partners)
Register of Transfers of Partnership Interests
Register of General Partner Resolutions and Minutes Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 - USD 5,000 per year for registered office and professional registered agent/compliance services in Luxembourg
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 10,000 per year if the statutory audit threshold is triggered; no audit fee required for a small SCSp below the thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City combined headline: 17% corporate income tax + 0.7% solidarity surcharge on CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax; an SCSp is fiscally transparent unless it validly opts into corporate taxation, in which case the combined headline rate applies at entity level)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday is available. Principal preferential deductions: IP Box exemption of 80% for qualifying patent and software IP income; participation exemption of 100% for qualifying dividends and capital gains; notional interest deduction on qualifying new equity capital; reduced corporate rate of 20% (before solidarity and municipal tax) for the first EUR 200,000 of taxable income of an opted-in entity. For a transparent SCSp, tax is levied at partner level and no Luxembourg entity-level CIT applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 800 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités); e-filed through the Luxembourg direct tax portal 'eC1' accessible via MyGuichet.lu
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly provisional CIT instalments may be imposed by assessment notice
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year SCSp the default due date is 30 June of the following year. The Luxembourg Tax Administration (ACD) may grant an extension on written application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identification: RCSL registration number, Luxembourg tax matricule, legal form 'SCSp', registered office, and eC1 portal account reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners must provide a Luxembourg tax representative if the SCSp has no local management; include the representative's identification and mandate reference.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year opening and closing dates; first period may exceed 12 months for a newly incorporated SCSp.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should align the SCSp profit allocation schedule with their home country tax year and attach the partnership deed profit-sharing percentages.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net result before tax adjustments: gross turnover from canned boba tapioca pearls and aseptic tubing services, cost of goods sold, depreciation, provisions, and operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a transparent SCSp, report only Luxembourg-source items; exclude each partner's non-Luxembourg income and attach a partner profit allocation statement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments: reinstatement of non-deductible expenses (fines, excessive interest, certain taxes) and deduction of exempt income and prior-year losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners may only offset Luxembourg PE-source losses against Luxembourg-source income; losses are carried forward 17 years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of net taxable income after loss carryforward and application of participation exemption or IP box relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner with no Luxembourg permanent establishment does not file Form 800 solely because it holds an interest in a transparent SCSp; the partner reports its allocable share in its home jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: prepayments, withholding tax credits, foreign tax credits, and DTA relief computations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner claiming treaty relief must attach a home-state TRC, provide the SCSp allocation certificate, and submit the claim through the annual refund procedure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Administrative fine from EUR 100 to EUR 25,000; 10% late-filing surcharge on the total tax due, increased to 20% for repeat non-filing; late-payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month (7.2% per annum); fraudulent filings trigger criminal sanctions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 820 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur la fortune); only required where the SCSp has opted into Luxembourg corporate taxation and holds taxable Luxembourg assets; e-filed via eC1/MyGuichet.lu
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same filing window as Form 800, normally within six months after the fiscal year-end, with extension available on request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net wealth base: total Luxembourg-situs assets less liabilities, including equipment, inventory of canned boba pearls, bank balances, and receivables.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A transparent SCSp is not a separate net wealth taxpayer; non-resident partners include their pro-rata share in their own Luxembourg net wealth return only if they have a Luxembourg taxable nexus.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exemptions: substantial shareholding participation exemption, restructuring exemption, and statutory allowance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a schedule of exempt participations and the percentage held directly or indirectly by each non-resident partner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable net wealth and amount to carry to the eC1 assessment cover.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Home jurisdictions granting foreign tax credit relief will accept the ACD assessment notice as proof of Luxembourg net wealth tax borne.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Same penalty regime as Form 800: 0.6% monthly interest, 10% surcharge, fine up to EUR 25,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 400/410 (Déclaration pour l'impôt commercial communal / municipal business tax), filed with the ACD through eC1 for the commune where the SCSp maintains its commercial establishment
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly prepayments may be required by commune assessment notice
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the close of the fiscal year, aligned with the Form 800 deadline; extension granted by the ACD applies to both returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross operating receipts allocable to the Luxembourg permanent establishment: canned boba tapioca sales, aseptic tubing fees, and related export revenues.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Luxembourg commercial activity; receipts attributable to foreign establishments or foreign sales activities outside Luxembourg must be excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses: production costs, raw tapioca starch procurement, wages of manufacturing personnel, depreciation of aseptic tubing lines, and general overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must not deduct home-office expenses incurred in their own jurisdiction against Luxembourg municipal business tax income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Municipal business income after statutory allowances, loss carryforward, and application of arm's-length transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a transfer pricing summary if related-party transactions exceeded the EUR 1,000,000 local-file threshold.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing and late-payment penalties mirror CIT: 0.6% monthly interest, 10% surcharge, and administrative fine up to EUR 25,000; repeated non-compliance may lead to withdrawal of the commune's business licence.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% standard Luxembourg dividend withholding tax for distributions by corporate payers. Distributions by an SCSp are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax because the SCSp is fiscally transparent and is not a legal entity subject to CIT; where an SCSp receives dividends, 15% may be withheld at the underlying corporate payer, reducible to 0% under the Luxembourg participation exemption or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where conditions are met.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Double Tax Agreement, the beneficial owner must file Form 250 (refund or at-source relief request) with the ACD, attach the original or certified home-state TRC for the relevant tax year, and evidence of beneficial ownership and holding period. For an SCSp, each partner applies separately in proportion to its allocable share and must attach the SCSp's partnership deed, partner allocation statement, and extract from the Luxembourg trade register. The ACD generally processes at-source relief before distribution or issues a refund within six to twelve months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law does not impose withholding tax on outbound interest or royalty payments (statutory 0%). Treaty rates on inbound Luxembourg-source interest and royalties typically range from 0% to 10% depending on the DTA and limitation-of-benefits provisions. Arm's-length pricing must be evidenced for IP royalties related to boba manufacturing and aseptic tubing technology.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and transfer pricing documentation are mandatorily required when intra-group transactions with related parties exceed EUR 1,000,000 per fiscal year; Master File is required when the global group consolidated revenue exceeds EUR 750,000,000. Below the threshold, the SCSp must still retain contemporaneous evidence to substantiate arm's-length pricing upon ACD request.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not operate standalone Economic Substance Regulations, but economic substance is enforced through the OECD BEPS precondition, EU ATAD GAAR, Luxembourg's abuse-of-law doctrine, and the ACD's practice governing tax residence certificates. A manufacturing SCSp must demonstrate real substance in Luxembourg: actual production and aseptic tubing capacity, qualified employees, decision-making by Luxembourg-based managers, local bank accounts, and adequate capitalisation. Absent substance, the ACD may deny treaty benefits, reclassify the SCSp as a taxable resident company, and disregard the partnership's separate existence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inflating deductible costs for tapioca starch imports, understating canned boba export revenue, fabricating invoices for aseptic tubing services, or filing false Form 800/820 statements with the ACD.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 10% to 50% of the under-assessed tax under LIR Articles 119-120; administrative fine up to EUR 25,000; monthly late-payment interest at 0.6%; criminal conviction may lead to imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to twice the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, general partners, and beneficial owners who knowingly sign or direct false filings are jointly and severally liable for the company's tax debts, interest, and penalties; criminal courts may impose travel bans, prohibition on holding corporate mandates, and custodial sentences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SCSp as a shell with only a registered office and bank account, having no manufacturing employees or aseptic tubing operations, placing effective management outside Luxembourg, and relying on Luxembourg tax transparency and treaty network to shelter undisclosed profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation and reassessment under the Luxembourg abuse-of-law rule (LIR Art. 6) and ATAD GAAR; denial of tax residence certificates and DTA benefits; disregard of the SCSp's separate legal personality; restated taxable profits in the hands of the actual owner; additional tax, interest, and penalties up to 25% of the reassessed amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and indirect shareholders may be personally assessed for unpaid corporate and municipal tax; repeated abuse can trigger criminal sanctions, asset forfeiture, and travel bans against the orchestrating individuals.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing cash proceeds from boba tapioca sales through the SCSp account without supporting commercial contracts, accepting wire transfers from unidentified counterparties, or issuing false Swift LC and TT wire documentation to disguise the origin of funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the amended Law of 12 November 2004 and the Criminal Code, money laundering is punishable by imprisonment of six months to five years and fines for natural persons; legal persons face fines up to EUR 5,000,000, confiscation of proceeds, publication of the judgment, and potential withdrawal of the manufacturer's/export licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally criminally liable where they knew or should reasonably have known of the laundering; courts may issue travel bans, freezing orders on personal assets, and disqualification from commercial management.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting non-arm's-length prices for raw tapioca starch purchased from a related supplier, undercharging a related distributor of canned boba pearls, or booking excessive royalties for aseptic tubing technology without a benchmark study.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income under LIR Art. 164 and OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines; disallowance of excessive deductions; penalty for negligent misdeclaration up to 50% of the adjustment; 0.6% monthly interest; administrative fine up to EUR 25,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve false transfer pricing documentation may be held jointly and severally liable for the additional tax, interest, and penalties; intentional mispricing linked to fraud can lead to criminal liability and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Total Failure to File or Persistent Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Complete omission of Form 800, Form 820, or municipal business tax Form 400/410 after production and aseptic tubing operations commence in Luxembourg, or failure to file the SCSp annual partner information return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 10% surcharge on the total assessed tax, 0.6% monthly interest, fine up to EUR 25,000; ACD may proceed to official assessment, forced collection, and revocation of business registration; repeated non-filing is treated as criminal tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant or manager of the general partner is personally liable for unpaid tax debts arising from intentional or grossly negligent non-filing; personal bank accounts may be attached, and a travel ban may be imposed where flight risk or asset dissipation is demonstrated.
